Magical gene / ground and strong white

Cleave

The horse split about half and half along a boundary made of interlocking spears - long narrow triangles driven into each field from the other, never a curve anywhere - edged in a half-opaque outline where the two meet. Which half the split claims is the allele: Cleave takes the front of the horse, Waves the back.

Finding one

About 1 in 1,786 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

Its gene carrot

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/cleave.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

Keyhorsegenetics.cleave
Phasemagical — it adds signed colour in phase 3, after the pigment has resolved
Priority202 — where it sits in the one (priority, key) paint order
AllelesClv · Clc · Wav · Wac · n
Varies per horse5 values drawn once off the expressing allele copy, so a foal that inherits the copy inherits the look
Built fromAXIS, SPOTS, TOWARD, WAVES

Why it is built this way

The detached spears used to be fat ovals (radius 1.3, stretch 2.4) scattered over a band up to 42% of the horse long, which read as random white splotches loose on the far half rather than as spears thrown clear of the boundary (owner's call). They are now long and thin (radius 0.55, stretch 4.2) and the band they sit in is tied close behind the line, because 'reach' was narrowed to 0.30-0.40 against a split of 0.42-0.60. 'reach' stays strictly below the split's minimum so the band can never invert its own from/to.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Cleave

White and coat take about half the horse each - between 45 and 55 per cent, never outside 35 to 65. White has the front: the head, the front and underside of the neck, the chest, the forelegs and the front of the shoulder; the coat keeps the withers, back, croup, hindquarters and hind legs. What makes it Cleave is the boundary: each field drives long narrow triangles into the other, straight along the sides and never convex, with smaller teeth splitting off the flanks of the big ones and the pattern of them different on the two sides. Detached spears of the same shape float within a hand's span of the line. Where the two meet, a half-opaque outline in the same colour runs along the whole edge - the one soft thing on the horse. Everything else is hard: no gradient, no roaning, no feathering anywhere.

  1. the front half, and the straight-sided teeth it drives into the other — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  2. a half-opaque outline where the front half meets the coat — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  3. detached spears floating clear of the line — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Coloured Cleave

The same front-half interlock, with the near half in a colour the line carries rather than in white. Recessive to the white form but dominant over both Waves alleles: two copies, or one beside a Waves copy, and it is the Cleave side that shows. It never gives blue eyes.

  1. the front half, and the straight-sided teeth it drives into the other, in colour — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  2. a half-opaque outline where the front half meets the coat, in colour — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  3. detached spears floating clear of the line, in colour — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Waves

The identical split, reversed end for end - which is the whole of what used to be a second gene. White has the back: the croup, the hindquarters, the hind legs and the tail; the coat keeps the shoulder, the neck, the head and the forelegs. What makes it Cleave is the boundary: each field drives long narrow triangles into the other, straight along the sides and never convex, with smaller teeth splitting off the flanks of the big ones and the pattern of them different on the two sides. Detached spears of the same shape float within a hand's span of the line. Where the two meet, a half-opaque outline in the same colour runs along the whole edge - the one soft thing on the horse. Everything else is hard: no gradient, no roaning, no feathering anywhere.

  1. the back half, and the straight-sided teeth it drives into the other — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  2. a half-opaque outline where the back half meets the coat — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  3. detached spears floating clear of the line — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD

Coloured Waves

The reversed split with the caudal half in a colour the line carries rather than in white. The most recessive of the four: it takes two copies. It never gives blue eyes.

  1. the back half, and the straight-sided teeth it drives into the other, in colour — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  2. a half-opaque outline where the back half meets the coat, in colour — WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES × WAVES, painted with TOWARD
  3. detached spears floating clear of the line, in colour — SPOTS × AXIS, painted with TOWARD
